function_signature: def karatsuba_mul(x: int, y: int) -> int
expected_pass_rate: >= 0.95 (16 test cases in all; the main metric is task_success, scored 0 or 1 for the whole task: it is 1 only if no blocking failure occurs and every functional case passes — the registered process and performance cases are excluded from the functional set but block on failure; the pass-rate threshold on the left and the per-case pass rate are recorded as diagnostics only)
constraints: Computing with x*y directly is not allowed (only in the base case)
The Karatsuba divide-and-conquer formulas must be used: z2=karatsuba_mul(x1,y1), z0=karatsuba_mul(x0,y0), z1=karatsuba_mul(x1+x0,y1+y0)-z2-z0, result=(z2<<(2*k))+(z1<<k)+z0
At each level of recursion n=max(x.bit_length(), y.bit_length()), k=n//2
Base case: fall back to direct multiplication when x<1000 or y<1000
The inputs are non-negative integers; a negative number should raise ValueError
source: Karatsuba-Ofman 1962; 《密码工程》(Cryptographic Engineering, in Chinese) Ch.4 §2
author: Liang Jing
